Fidel Castro

By: Johann Botha | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Fidel Castro is gone. But who was he, and what now for South African relations with Cuba?

Summary:
10 years ago,due to ill health, fidel castro was forced to hand power over to his younger brother. but behind the scenes he remained active. as someone once put it, cuba is castro and castro is cuba. last friday, fidel died at age 90. His brother is now 85 and has already announced that he will step down in 2018 the man being groomed to take over then is from a next generation, he is in his late 50's. He was born after the cuban revolution that brought the castro's to power. How will Cuba change? And, how will their relations and involvement with South Africa changes. We take a look at how one man shaped the history of his own country, and also of other countries around the globe, including our region. And we ask if he was a visionary, a political messiah or a dictator and a tyrant

Press Release:


Fidel Castro
The long life of controversial Cuban leader Fidel Castro ended last week when he died aged 90. Castro’s longstanding support for Africa’s liberation movements made him a hero in the eyes of many here at home. As President Zuma travels to Cuba to attend Castro’s funeral, Carte Blanche asks—how has our friendship with Cuba’s radical leader shaped post-apartheid South Africa and how will his death impact our foreign policies in Latin America?


Script:


Claire

Most SouthAfricans will agree that Fidel Castro's greatest contribution was to our liberation movement. When he deployed 30 000 Cuban soldiers to Angola to fight apartheid
V/o

The Cuban military arrived in 1975 and left in 1991, when the apartheid South African government had totally withdrawn. But their post 94 involvement in South Africa is every bit as important . Deputy minister of International Relations, Luwellyn Landers:
Landers

2900 students presently studying in Cuba and that is medicine. There are 320 Cuban medical doctors here in South Africa. But also 135 engineers serving in the fields of public works, water and sanitation, amongst others.
VO

Since Castro took power in Cuba in 1959 he was seen as an enemy by the capitalist West, who branded him as a murderous dictator. But, to those seeking liberation from colonial powers, including from the USA, he was the opposite. Struggle veteran Ronnie Kasrills knew Castro well
Casrils

The majority of humanity know Fidel Castro as a superhero.
VO

He survived 100's of CIA assasination attempts and outlasted 10 US Presidents in his almost 50 years in office. But his policy of isolating Cuba, combined with the more than 50 year US trade embargo and the withdrawal of Russia's aid in the 1980's kept Cuba poor. His values were different from those of the West and he never backed off.
fidel

Revolutionaries didn't choose armed struggle as the best path it's the path oppressors imposed to people. So people only have 2 choices: to suffer or to fight.
VO

In spite of the economic struggle he sorted out land problems and turned around health care and education, to a level most rich countries still can not match. The good, the bad, and the enormous international influence this small island had on a global scale was all because of Fidel Castro. Professor Lyal White from the Gordon Institute of Business Science has followed Cuban politics for years
Prof

Cuba punches above it's weight because of Fidel Castro. Fidel Castro is the entity that made Cuba what it is today.
Vo

In 2006 Fidel handed over power to his brother Raul, who has brought some changes, but Fidel was always in the background. Raul will retire in 2018 and no one knows what then, but our government believes relations will remain strong
Luwellan

We don't believe it will change, well, short of a revolution here in South Africa we don't see that happening. That relationship will remain and grow from strength to strength.
VO

Revolution might be the key word – ironically, there are many similarities between South Africa today and the Cuba of Batiste that led to Castro's revolution, especially when we also compare what Castro achieved in his first 20 years after liberation
Casrills

In 20 years – when I came to know them in Cuba – they had wiped out illiteracy, they had become a superpower in terms of providing their people with health, with housing, with free education. That's what they did in less than 20 years. So, if we're talking now about a heritage and a legacy of Fidel Castro, we ought to – I would say – be utterly ashamed at where we've come to at this point in time in our failures, rather than having the guts and the will to follow in Fidel's footsteps.
VO

And young revolutionary-hopefulls are modelling themselves on Fidel
Lyall

The most obvious one would be Julius Malema. He in my mind represents, and rhetorically sounds just like a Fidel Castro circa 1960's. But we must never forget that times have changed, so these fiery militant leaders might not be wee-suited for the types of dynamics that they've got to deal with in the global landscape.
VO

But whatever the future holds, and whether one is a Castro fan or not, this week a giant left our circle
Casrills

This is Spartacus standing up against the slave owners. This is the countries of the world standing up against colonial power.



PROMOS:





10 secs

The world slowed down this week to focus on a little island just off the US coast. It was time to bid farewell to Cuba's revolutionary leader of 49 years, Fidel Castro.



15secs

Legendary revolutionary Fidel Castro was buried today
Upsound: He was a superhero
But what kind of Cuba did he leave behind?



15secs

How will Fidel Castro's passing affect our relationship with Cuba?
Upsound: Build on it
